source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne's San Antonio campus publishes 33 MW of IT capacity across two facilities, placing it among Texas's top tier of disclosed data centers and representing 6.9% of the state's stated 475 MW total.

At standard AI training density of 40 kW per rack, this campus could accommodate roughly 825 racks. At the higher power draw of GPU-dense inference workloads, around 100 kW per rack, capacity drops to approximately 330 racks. These figures matter because they constrain which workload types the facility can support given its power envelope.

The six published certifications—SOC 2 Type 2, PCI DSS, HIPAA, FISMA, and TIA-942—indicate this campus is built primarily for regulated enterprise and government workloads rather than commercial AI training. The combination of compliance scope suggests the architecture prioritizes security and data isolation over the sustained high-power utilization that large AI clusters demand.

Texas has 133 mapped data center facilities but only 19 disclose IT load figures. This 85 percent gap between mapped and published counts means the state's actual computing capacity is largely unknown. CyrusOne San Antonio is one of the few operators willing to state power capacity, which makes its ranking visible but leaves most of the state's infrastructure opaque.
